stem: Cobalt, rhodium and iridium are metals in the same group of the Periodic Table.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: The shorthand electronic configuration of cobalt is $[\text{Ar}]3\text{d}^74\text{s}^2$.
parts.text: Identify what is meant by $[\text{Ar}]$ by giving its full electronic configuration.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The lowest-energy electrons in cobalt are in the $1\text{s}$ orbital.

Draw the shape of a $1\text{s}$ orbital.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Deduce the number of unpaired electrons in a cobalt atom.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Table 1.1 gives some details of the stable naturally occurring isotopes of rhodium and iridium.

Table 1.1

| isotope | number of protons | number of neutrons | total number of electron shells |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $^{103}_{45}\text{Rh}$ |  | 58 |  |
| $^{191}_{77}\text{Ir}$ |  |  | 6 |
| $^{193}_{77}\text{Ir}$ |  |  | 6 |

Complete Table 1.1.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
Table 1.2 shows the relative abundances of isotopes in a sample of an alloy containing rhodium and iridium only.

Table 1.2

| isotope | relative isotopic mass | relative abundance in alloy |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $^{103}_{45}\text{Rh}$ | 102.91 | 50.00 |
| $^{191}_{77}\text{Ir}$ | 190.96 | 15.18 |
| $^{193}_{77}\text{Ir}$ | 192.96 | 34.82 |

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Use Table 1.2 to calculate the relative atomic mass, $A_r$, of iridium in the alloy.

Give your answer to **two** decimal places.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
Hydrated rhodium(III) chloride, $\text{RhCl}_3\cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$, catalyses the conversion of ethene to but-2-ene.

Both stereoisomers of but-2-ene are formed in the reaction.
parts.text:
Hydrated rhodium(III) chloride contains 20.5% by mass of water of crystallisation.

Deduce the integer value of $x$ in $\text{RhCl}_3\cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

Show your working.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Explain how the conversion of ethene to but-2-ene can be described as an addition reaction.
